messages:
cassie: Quick design question — we need to lock down console + API semantics for plan-aware routing + variant failover before I start the policy editor work. Prefer a short sync here so we don't mismatch behavior across hosted/dedicated/private.
jorge: SG. what's the high level you want? priority order, enforcement, telemetry?
cassie: Exactly. Proposed priorities:
  1) region affinity (if tenant pinned region, prefer that)
  2) plan routing rules (enterprise -> dedicated variants; pro -> standard; free -> best-effort)
  3) variant compatibility fallback chain (same architecture quantized -> alternate quant -> cheaper model)
  4) quota enforcement: soft degrade for free/pro, hard for enterprise (unless tenant opts-in to degrade)
anita: soft vs hard is detaily. can we define "soft degrade" as returning a compatible-but-cheaper variant with a warning header + metric? :thinking_face:
kevin: +1. Important: API must be explicit about when we demote. Clients need headers/sparse telemetry to decide whether to retry or not.
marta: For console UX, we should offer two things: a per-plan preset (defaults) and an "advanced" JSON editor for system teams. Most folks will use presets.
cassie: Right. Also need a clear fallback_reason tag on every response: e.g. fallback_reason=region_unavailable | variant_mismatch | quota_soft_limit | quota_hard_block. That feeds alerts and quality regressions.
jorge: How do we handle quota windows? immediate hard block or leaky bucket with buffer?
cassie: Proposal:
  - free: soft_window=30s, soft_threshold=90% of burst, allow demote to cheaper model for up to 20% of requests, emit metric fallback_rate
  - pro: soft_window=15s, demote allowance 10%, emit fallback_rate + cost_delta
  - enterprise: default hard_block=true, but tenant can enable degrade_mode=true to allow demote instead of reject
anita: Can we add a small grace countdown header so client UIs can show "degrading for 00:12"? header name: X-RW-Fallback-Expiry
kevin: Need to avoid too many headers. Prefer a single JSON metadata blob in response when a fallback occurs. e.g. ```
"routing": {"chosen_variant":"rw-gpt-3a-q4", "fallback_reason":"quota_soft_limit", "region":"us-west-2", "expires_at":"2025-07-12T15:23:00Z"}
```

kevin: That should be in response metadata, not in-stream tokens.
marta: Console: show per-plan summary: fallback_rate, avg_cost_delta, p95_latency, current_rollout (canary %), and a toggle "allow automatic demotion" per plan.
cassie: Agree. For backend policy schema I was thinking of adding a new top-level field routing_policy with something like:
```
{
  "routing_policy": {
    "plan_defaults": {
      "free": {"allow_demote": true, "demote_budget_pct": 20, "soft_window_s": 30},
      "pro": {"allow_demote": true, "demote_budget_pct": 10, "soft_window_s": 15},
      "enterprise": {"allow_demote": false}
    },
    "fallback_chain": ["same-region-compatible", "cross-region-compatible", "quantized-compatible", "cheaper-model"],
    "telemetry_keys": ["fallback_reason","route_choice","variant_promotion"]
  }
}
```
cassie: That exact object will need to be normalized into the API contract. Thoughts on default fallback_chain order?
jorge: Looks fine. I would prefer "cross-region-compatible" after "quantized-compatible" to preserve QoS — network might kill latency.
anita: +1 to Jorge. If we fall to cross-region we should only do it for non-interactive workloads (embeddings/batch) unless tenant allows higher latency.
kevin: So add route constraints by workload_type. We'll need to expose that in policy and keep console simple (auto-detect workload type from route config).
marta: UX note: when a tenant changes plan_defaults we should warn about billing/cost changes. show an estimated cost delta for enabling demotion on enterprise.
cassie: Telemetry: collect these events per request: route_choice, fallback_reason, from_variant, to_variant, cost_before, cost_after, latency_ms. Those feed alerts when fallback_rate > 1% for a tenant.
jorge: What about rollouts? We should support canary by plan: e.g. enable fallback_chain v2 for 5% of enterprise traffic. Console shows canary % and a kill switch.
cassie: Yep. That means routing decision needs to consult rollout flags. Implementation note: keep decision fast (inlined in gateway) and offload complex eval to sidecar for non-blocking sampling.
anita: Security/compliance: private deployments need full parity but allow customer-managed policies. ensure policy schema is versioned.
kevin: Implementation tasks: 1) API contract + schema; 2) runtime fast-path decision logic; 3) telemetry events + alerting; 4) console presets + advanced editor; 5) rollout UI
cassie: I'll draft the API change and a small PR with schema samples. I'll also add unit tests for decision matrix.
deploy-bot: deploy-1.4.8 started to canary (eng-platform) — uid 0a1b2c
jorge: Thanks all. Cassie — if you post the PR link I'll review the schema bits.
cassie: Will do. Posting follow-up doc in #docs once PR is up. :thumbsup:
